subject: Post-demo: procurement & pricing path for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jason Lee <jason.lee@acmepayments.com>, procurement@acmepayments.com
Date: 2026-11-08T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement & pricing path for Acme Payments

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the walk-through of your use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the commercial + procurement path: 

What we covered:
- Recommended deployment options: hosted (fast POC), dedicated (predictable throughput + isolation), private (VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads).
- Pricing levers: committed reserved capacity (discounts for monthly/annual commits) vs on-demand (pay-as-you-go for pilots).
- Integration/marketplace: we can support purchases via card, PO, and in many cases via cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP) depending on procurement rules.

Actions / Qs for Acme procurement:
1) Who is the procurement contact we should loop in for PO terms and tax/accounting details?
2) Do you typically issue a PO for pilots or only for production contracts (thresholds)?
3) Any interest in purchasing via AWS Marketplace or do you prefer direct contract/PO?

I've attached:
- pricing-sheet.xlsx (summary of hosted/dedicated/private price bands)
- procurement-checklist.pdf (what procurement typically asks for: SOC2, contract template, billing contact, PO instructions)

If it works, propose a short procurement Q&A (30 min) next week to align on PO vs card and whether AWS Marketplace helps your process.

Thanks — looping in Aditya (solutions) to add a quick note on packaging/commit options.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great session. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- We typically require a PO for anything over $50k ARR; smaller pilots are usually on corporate card. That said, procurement will still want contract terms reviewed for pilots that touch production data.
- We have a procurement lead, Samantha Ruiz (cc'd), who manages PO intake and contract review.
- We are evaluating using AWS Marketplace for some purchases; if Redwood is listed there and supports consolidated billing, that could speed approval, but we need to confirm whether PO workflows are supported through the marketplace for our finance processes.

Can Samantha confirm whether she prefers a direct SOW and PO to billing@redwood.com or whether marketplace would be preferable?

On the technical side, we'll want to validate the dedicated option's SLA and data controls if we move beyond pilot.

Best,

Hi Jason / Marissa — quick note from solutions to help with procurement questions and packaging guidance: 

Short answers:
- Marketplace: yes, we support AWS Marketplace and can enable purchases there. For PO workflows, there are two options: (1) customer issues PO directly to Redwood for a direct contract, or (2) purchases via AWS Marketplace use consolidated billing but procurement processes vary — some customers still require a PO referencing the marketplace invoice. We can work with your finance team to map the right flow.
- PO vs card: typical approach is card for pilot (<$50k) and PO for production/committed deals. If you prefer to do a pilot on commit structure, we can offer a small short-term commit with a credit against future consumption.
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private:
  * Hosted: fastest to start, pay-as-you-go; limited isolation but good for early validation.
  * Dedicated: reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and isolation (recommended for production ML workloads that need consistent latency). Commits provide better unit economics here.
  * Private: full VPC or on-prem option for data residency/regulatory requirements; typically involves an enterprise contract and longer procurement lead time.

Attached: SOW-draft.docx (template) and pricing-breakdown.pdf (example commit vs on-demand math).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marissa to loop in procurement lead (Samantha) and finance contact so we can confirm PO thresholds and preferred purchasing mechanism.
2) If Acme prefers marketplace, we'll confirm listing details and provide marketplace SKU/pricing.
3) If leaning to Dedicated with a commit, we'll send a short-term commit offer (30–90 days) to cover pilot usage and apply credit toward the annual commit if you decide to proceed.

Happy to jump on the procurement call and walk through the SOW and billing flow.

— Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
